items.text: Hobbes argued humans are naturally selfish; Rousseau argued humans are naturally good. Which view better matches reality?

options.A: Hobbes is clearly correct—humans are fundamentally self-interested
options.B: Hobbes is mostly correct, with some exceptions
options.C: Both have merit—humans have both good and evil tendencies
options.D: Rousseau is mostly correct, with some exceptions
options.E: Rousseau is clearly correct—humans are fundamentally good

items.text: When social constraints are removed and people can act without consequences, most will:

options.B: Act selfishly but avoid actively harming others
options.C: Behave much as they normally do—constraints don't change nature
options.E: Reveal their natural goodness and cooperativeness

items.text: In the aftermath of a natural disaster, which response is more representative of "true" human nature?

options.C: Both looting and helping occur—humans are morally mixed
options.D: Spontaneous cooperation is more common than selfishness
options.E: Humans reliably form rescue teams and help strangers
